digo_source: Pakia 2005 Appendix III ('Mkoko bara'; 'hinterland mkoko', not classed among mikoko)

teaser.en: Its Digo name calls it a mangrove of the mainland, yet the Digo do not count it among the mangroves at all.

summary.en: *Mkoko bara*, the white milkwood, is an evergreen tree with milky sap and dark berries that grows in bushland and dune thicket behind the shore. Its name is a small lesson in how Digo plant names work.

about.en:
*Mkoko bara* is an evergreen coastal tree, often shrubby and dense in exposed places, with thick, leathery dark-green leaves. Break a leaf or twig and it bleeds white, milky latex, which is where the English name milkwood comes from.

Its small flowers are greenish-white and clustered along the stems, and they are followed by round berries that ripen to dark purple or black. The berries are eaten by birds.

where.en: Despite its name, it does not grow in the tidal mud. Look for it in coastal bushland and dune thicket just behind the shore, where wind and salt spray shape the trees into low, rounded crowns.

uses.en: No particular uses have been recorded for it among the Digo so far.

culture.en: The name joins *mkoko*, mangrove, with *bara*, the mainland or hinterland: roughly 'the inland mangrove'. Yet the Digo do not count it among the *mikoko*. Pakia uses it as an example of how a shared name does not mean a shared category: the tree borrows the mangrove's name without belonging to the mangrove family of trees.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *mkoko bara*, the 'hinterland *mkoko*'. The Mgombato dictionary gives *mkoko* (plural *mikoko*) as mangrove or mangrove pole, used in building. No Swahili name has been recorded. In English it is the white milkwood, and its scientific name is *Sideroxylon inerme*.

reason.en: The true mkoko, the red mangrove
Grows in the same thicket behind the shore

mgombato: mkoko1 (mi) mangrove, mangrove pole (used in building); mkoko.
sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
